title: Methyl jasmonate mitigates cisplatin-induced nephrotoxicity via modulation of Caspase-3/COX-2/ NF-kappaB signalling pathway: In silico, In vitro, and In vivo investigations.
authors: Katolkar, Ujwal N; Surana, Sanjay J
one_liner_zh: 该研究用分子对接和实验探究茉莉酸甲酯对顺铂肾毒性的保护作用，虽含蛋白-配体对接，但对象为小分子-蛋白而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Cisplatin is a widely used chemotherapeutic agent; however, its clinical utility is limited due to several organ toxicities, including nephrotoxicity, which is primarily mediated through oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis. This study examines the protective effect of methyl jasmonate (MeJA) in mitigating cisplatin-induced nephrotoxicity by modulating the caspase-3/COX-2/NF-kappaB signaling pathway. Initially, we performed molecular docking to evaluate the binding affinity of MeJA against the caspase-3, cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2), and nuclear factor kappa B (NF-kappaB) proteins in the presence of the reference drug amifostine. Further, in vitro cell cytotoxicity on Madin-Darby canine kidney (MDCK) cells via MTT assay, oxidative stress, and proinflammatory markers. We have also performed an in vivo analysis of MeJA on cisplatin-induced nephrotoxicity in experimental rats by employing several biochemical parameters and histopathological investigation on rat kidney tissues. In silico molecular docking analysis revealed strong binding interactions between MeJA, key apoptotic and inflammatory mediators, suggesting its potential to regulate cisplatin-induced toxicity. In vitro studies using MDCK cells demonstrated that MeJA significantly reduced cisplatin-induced cytotoxicity, oxidative stress, and proinflammatory markers. In vivo experiments in rats further confirmed the nephroprotective effects of MeJA, as evidenced by improved renal function markers, and histopathological preservation of renal tubules and glomerulus tissues of rat kidneys. While ELISA testing revealed that MeJA downregulates caspase-3 and COX-2 expression and suppresses NF-kappaB activation. These findings collectively highlight the therapeutic potential of MeJA in alleviating cisplatin-induced nephrotoxicity through modulation of apoptosis and inflammatory pathways. MeJA may serve as a promising nephroprotective agent, warranting further clinical investigation for its potential application in oncology settings.
abstract_zh: 顺铂是一种广泛使用的化疗药物；然而，其临床应用受到多种器官毒性的限制，包括肾毒性，这主要通过氧化应激、炎症和细胞凋亡介导。本研究探讨了茉莉酸甲酯（MeJA）通过调节caspase-3/COX-2/NF-kappaB信号通路来减轻顺铂诱导的肾毒性的保护作用。首先，我们进行了分子对接，以评估MeJA在参考药物氨磷汀存在下与caspase-3、环氧合酶-2（COX-2）和核因子kappa B（NF-kappaB）蛋白的结合亲和力。进一步，通过MTT法对Madin-Darby犬肾（MDCK）细胞进行了体外细胞毒性、氧化应激和促炎标志物的检测。我们还通过多种生化参数和对大鼠肾组织的组织病理学检查，对实验大鼠中MeJA对顺铂诱导的肾毒性进行了体内分析。计算机模拟分子对接分析揭示了MeJA与关键凋亡和炎症介质之间的强结合相互作用，表明其具有调节顺铂诱导毒性的潜力。使用MDCK细胞的体外研究表明，MeJA显著降低了顺铂诱导的细胞毒性、氧化应激和促炎标志物。大鼠体内实验进一步证实了MeJA的肾保护作用，表现为肾功能标志物改善，以及大鼠肾脏肾小管和肾小球组织的组织病理学保存。ELISA检测显示，MeJA下调caspase-3和COX-2表达，并抑制NF-kappaB激活。这些发现共同强调了MeJA通过调节凋亡和炎症通路来缓解顺铂诱导肾毒性的治疗潜力。MeJA可能作为一种有前景的肾保护剂，值得在肿瘤学环境中进一步临床研究其潜在应用。
